home.some-sakurascript-seriko-and-outfit-defi: Some SakuraScript, SERIKO, and outfit definitions are unsupported. Windows DLLs and executables do not run directly; some require a configured Wine environment.

home.check-release-notes-and-scan-reports: Check release notes and scan reports
home.ukagaka-is-a-system-and-culture-for-keep: Ukagaka is a system and culture for keeping characters on your desktop and enjoying their dialogue and reactions. The host app is called baseware; a character and its dialogue form a ghost; its appearance is a shell; and its speech window is a balloon. Utatane is baseware for macOS.
home.supported-yaya-aya-kagari-shiolink-miyoj: Supported YAYA (AYA), KAGARI, SHIOLINK (MiyoJS, etc.), SATORI, KAWARI, MISAKA, AKARI, ese-shiori, NiseShiori, Shino, Hisui, and Yuhna run without Wine. Rishu requires a separate Perl environment. Ghosts that depend on other Windows DLLs may still need Wine.
home.can-i-run-sakura-and-unyuu: Can I run Sakura and Unyuu?
home.the-supported-version-of-materia-s-first: The supported version of Materia’s first can run without Wine through a dedicated dialogue-data reader. It is not bundled; you need your own legitimately obtained files. This is not general-purpose Windows DLL execution.
home.the-app-and-this-page-support-japanese-e: The app and this page support Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Korean. Ghost dialogue stays in the author’s language and is not automatically translated.
home.please-report-the-ghost-s-name-your-utat: Please report the ghost’s name, your Utatane version, and what happened on GitHub Issues. Compatibility is still evolving, including rendering, text encoding, and events.
home.for-the-curious-alongside-sstp-and-rss-h: For the curious: alongside SSTP and RSS / HEADLINE support, there are experimental features for real-time voice conversations and AI integration.
home.the-app-is-released-under-the-mit-licens: The app is released under the MIT License. Ghosts, shells, and balloons are subject to their authors’ terms.
home.ria-s-shell-is-based-on-p016-nebusoku-by: Ria’s shell is based on “p016 (Nebusoku)” by BottleNeko. Balloon based on “something like Template” by lost-nd-xxx.

guide.title: Start with Ukagaka and Utatane — Find ghosts and understand compatibility
guide.description: Find Ukagaka ghost distribution sites and learn how Utatane compatibility differs from SSP.
guide.label: START HERE
guide.heading: Find ghosts. Understand the machinery.
guide.lead: For people new to Ukagaka and people moving from another baseware. App installation is covered on the overview page.
sections: Utatane is the “baseware,” the program that runs Ukagaka content. A “ghost” bundles a character, dialogue, and reactions. Shells change its appearance, balloons display dialogue, and releases commonly use the NAR archive format.

GHOST TOWN is a long-running database. Ghost Captor Sakura presents an image-rich update feed. Use Nise SiReFaSo to follow recent updates and Nise SoSiReMi to browse registered downloads. The Ukagaka Dream Team beginner guide is an English-language introduction.

Older databases contain discontinued or broken links. Follow through to the creator’s page and read its terms. Many releases are tested only with SSP, so Utatane compatibility varies by ghost.
Add a downloaded NAR with Utatane’s file picker, drag and drop, or Finder’s Open With command. See the overview download section for installing and opening the app itself.

AreaSSPninix-kagariUtatane
Primary OSWindowsLinux and WindowsmacOS 14 or later
PositionThe current de facto referenceA ninix-aya fork; major SHIORI can be built with itBuilt for macOS; major features in progress, not fully compatible
ModulesLoads Windows DLLs directlyLinux needs compatible SHIORI builds; SAORI is mainly ninix-saoriNative implementations first; some modules can use configured Wine
SetupWindows distributionBuild on Linux or use the Debian packageMac app; can import an extracted SSP folder

Support varies by environment; see the ninix-kagari project. For Utatane, see tested ghosts and remaining gaps.

Utatane identifies the dialogue engine (SHIORI) from files such as descript.txt, then connects YAYA, SATORI, KAWARI, MISAKA, and other known engines to separately installed macOS libraries. Supported SAORI libraries can be installed from the module catalog. Unsupported Windows DLLs run only when Wine and the helper host are configured.

State is kept outside the distributed ghost in Application Support. Even a supported engine does not guarantee every branch or Windows-specific dependency. Read Native SHIORI / SAORI for the technical details.
guide.trouble: If something does not work, report the ghost name, your Utatane version, and what happened on GitHub Issues. Compatibility is still in development, so not every ghost or feature is guaranteed to work.
